description: Southeast US deciduous woodlands. Rich forage, real winters in the north of range. Your first classroom.
name: Southeast Woodlands

fall.note: Harvest season. Nuts, persimmons, last greens. Fatten up.

spring.note: Greens return. Hungry season ends — if you make it.

summer.note: Berries, heat, snakes. Water is everywhere; food takes work.

winter.note: The boss. Nuts and stored food or nothing. Game gets bold.

description: Central European deciduous forest — beech, oak, hornbeam under a closed canopy, with meadow clearings, creek valleys, and the ruins of the people who managed it for centuries. Rich, seasonal, and honest: the mast feeds you in fall, the gap starves you in spring.
hazards: wild boar (all year — sows with young)
name: Temperate European Forest

fall.note: Mast season. Acorns, beechnuts, hazel, mushrooms. Fatten up — the gap is coming.

spring.note: The hungry gap ends here — wild garlic, first greens. Ticks wake up too.

summer.note: Berries, mushrooms after rain, heat in the clearings. Boar are bold.

winter.note: The boss. Nuts and stored food or nothing. The wolves come closer.

description: Towering terra firme forest, blackwater creeks, and floodplain that spends half the year underwater. Food hangs everywhere — if you know what you're looking at. The forest is not empty; it is a garden that forgot its gardeners.
hazards: flash floods in the wet season — the várzea goes under
fer-de-lance and other pit vipers in the leaf litter
mosquitoes at dusk (itchy; the giant ones carry worse)
jaguar near water at dusk and dawn
name: Amazon Rainforest

dry.note: Rivers drop. Fish crowd the shrinking pools — the hungry season for the forest, the harvest season for you.

wet.note: Rain most afternoons. Rivers flood the forest and the fish swim among the trees. Fruit everywhere; game dispersed.
